hook.text: How many people do you need in a room for a 50% chance two share a birthday? Just twenty-three.

buildup.text: With 365 possible birthdays, you'd expect to need way more people. Intuition screams 183 or so.

discovery.text: The trick: you're comparing every pair, not just one person to the rest. Pairs grow fast—23 people make 253.

twist.text: At 70 people the probability exceeds 99.9%. Near-certainty from a surprisingly small group.

climax.text: Humans underestimate combinatorial growth. We think linearly; probabilities compound exponentially.

quiz.question: Why does the birthday paradox seem surprising?
options: We underestimate the number of pairwise comparisons
